about.title: Ukiah Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a ladder collapses, a space heater sparks a fire, a car part gives out on Talmage Road or N State Street. In Mendocino County, Ukiah's mix of local retailers, agricultural equipment, and everyday consumer goods means defect injuries touch households across town. California generally applies strict liability to these cases, so an injured person often doesn't need to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product itself was flawed and that flaw caused harm. That covers design defects, manufacturing errors, and failure to warn. Several parties along the supply chain — makers, distributors, retailers — can share responsibility. If a defective product hurt you or someone in your family here in Ukiah, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney experienced in these claims so you can understand your options without added pressure.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the defect existed and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer who sold the product can potentially be held liable, which widens the options an attorney can explore on your behalf.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving the Product
items.desc: An independent attorney can advise you early on keeping the product, its packaging, and receipts intact, since physical evidence is often central to proving a defect claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving the company was careless. An attorney can explain how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me here in Ukiah?
items.answer: Try to keep the item exactly as it was when the injury happened, along with any packaging, instructions, or receipts. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, even if you're not sure yet whether you'll pursue a claim. This evidence can matter a great deal later.

items.question: Is there a cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You can explore your options without any upfront financial risk.
